title_hi: Feeling ko naam dena: kya research kehti hai?
topic: Affect labelling: controlled-task emotion-regulation evidence and limits
claim_classification: Controlled experimental evidence plus neuroimaging association; not a diagnostic or treatment claim

research.central_claim: In specific controlled laboratory tasks, putting an affective experience into words has been associated with lower reported distress relative to passive viewing; effects depend on experimental context.
limitations: The cited evidence does not show that labelling always calms a person or replaces support or treatment.
The reported fMRI differences are associations in task-specific samples, not proof that a word switches off a brain region.
One 2022 study reported different results by stimulus intensity, including increased distress in its lower-intensity condition.

sources.citation: Burklund et al. (2014), The common and distinct neural bases of affect labeling and reappraisal in healthy adults
Levy-Gigi & Shamay-Tsoory (2022), Affect labeling: The role of timing and intensity
Lieberman et al. (2007), Putting Feelings Into Words
